Paragraph:
Translation: Perform your prescribed duty, for action is better than inaction. A man cannot even maintain his physical body without work.

Purport (Excerpt): ...Lord Krsna did not want Arjuna to become a pretender, but that he perform his prescribed duties as set forth for ksatriyas... After all, one has to maintain one's body and soul together by some work. Work should not be given up capriciously, without purification of materialistic propensities...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The temptation to abandon functional responsibilities under stress or existential confusion.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna gives a direct imperative: Perform your prescribed duty (Niyattam kuru karma). Action is demonstrably better than inaction, as even basic physical survival requires work.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna receives a clear command to embrace active duty rather than escaping into passivity.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Behavioral Activation: Engaging in structured tasks to combat mental inertia and depression
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Fulfilling Core Responsibilities: Recognizing basic functional duties required to maintain life
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Avoiding Inertia: Choosing constructive activity over passive stagnation

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Niyata-karma (Prescribed, obligated duties according to one's nature/role)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Action is an essential cosmic law. Even bodily survival is impossible without work. Krishna instructs Arjuna to execute his duty as a warrior, as discharging obligatory duties purifies the heart and prevents spiritual regression.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Inaction and withdrawal often worsen mental distress, giving rise to depression and lethargy. 'Behavioral activation'—taking up structured, meaningful duties—is essential for mental health and physical maintenance. Doing your work, even when difficult, anchors the mind and builds resilience.
